Let $d$ be the degree of the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $P_x \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$. Then the absolute multiplicative height of $x$ is $H(x) = M(P_x)^{1/d}$, where $M(P_x)$ is the Mahler measure of $P_x$ regarded as a polynomial with complex coefficients.

nodes.summary: For every element $x$ of a field $K$ that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, the algebraic Mahler measure of $x$, that is the Mahler measure of the positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$, equals the Mahler measure of the primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$, both polynomials being regarded as polynomials with complex coefficients.
nodes.title: The sign normalization does not change the Mahler measure

nodes.summary: For an element $x$ of a field $K$ that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, the algebraic Mahler measure $M(x)$ is the Mahler measure of the positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$, regarded as a polynomial with complex coefficients. If $x$ is not algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$, this polynomial is the constant $1$, so $M(x) = 1$.
nodes.title: Algebraic Mahler measure

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be an element of a field $K$ that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $M(x)$ be its algebraic Mahler measure. If $M(x) > 1$, then $1 + \log M(x) < M(x)$.
nodes.title: One plus the logarithm of a Mahler measure above one is below it

nodes.summary: For every element $x$ of a field $K$ that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, the algebraic Mahler measure $M(x)$ of $x$ satisfies $1 \le M(x)$.
nodes.title: The algebraic Mahler measure is at least one

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $x \in K$ be algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then the positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$, with its integer coefficients mapped into $K$, vanishes at $x$.
nodes.title: An algebraic element is a root of its positive primitive integral minimal polynomial

nodes.summary: For every element $x$ of a field $K$ that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, the positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$ is primitive: the greatest common divisor of its integer coefficients is $1$.
nodes.title: The positive primitive integral minimal polynomial is primitive

nodes.summary: For every element $x$ of a field $K$ that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, the leading coefficient of the positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$ is a strictly positive integer.
nodes.title: The positive primitive integral minimal polynomial has positive leading coefficient

nodes.summary: The positive primitive integral minimal polynomial has the degree of the minimal polynomial. For every element $x$ of a field $K$ that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, the positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$ has the same degree as the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.title: The positive primitive integral minimal polynomial has the degree of the minimal polynomial

nodes.summary: For every element $x$ of a field $K$ that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, the positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$ has the same degree as the primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$.
nodes.title: Sign normalization preserves the degree

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field that is a $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra. For every $x \in K$, the positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$ is not the zero polynomial.
nodes.title: The positive primitive integral minimal polynomial is nonzero

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field that is a $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra, let $x \in K$, and let $p$ be the canonical primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$. The positive primitive integral minimal polynomial of $x$ is $-p$ if the leading coefficient of $p$ is negative, and $p$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Positive primitive integral minimal polynomial

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field that is an algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, let $x \in K$, and let $m_x \in \mathbb{Q}[X]$ be the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, with $m_x = 0$ when $x$ is not algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$. Choose a nonzero integer $b$ such that $b\,m_x$ has integer coefficients. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
